newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston hires Borden to head forex.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston hires Borden to head forex.

text.p: BankBoston said it hired James Borden, formerly a top foreign exchange executive at Chase Manhattan Bank, to head its foreign exchange unit.
BankBoston said Borden will be managing director of global foreign exchange. Borden will report to Brad Warner, Group Executive of Global treasury.

A spokeswoman for BankBoston said Thomas Hughes, who previously headed foreign exchange and derivatives, will now focus on derivatives. She said due to the rapid growth of the global treasury business, BankBoston is switching to more of a product focus from a geographic focus.

Before joining BankBoston, Borden was managing director of North American Foreign Exchange at Chase Manhattan. Earlier this year Chase was merged into Chemical Banking Corp which re-named itself the "new" Chase Manhattan Corp.

Borden began his career at Chase in 1964. He spent six years in the London office as an overseas eurocurrency funding manager and treasury manager. He was involved with global funding from 1976 to to 1980 and has been an executive in Chase's foreign exchange group for the past 16 years.

At Chase, Borden managed 75 foreign exchange professionals and was responsible for business development and risk management of all foreign exchange activities, including spot and forward trading, options and client advisory services.
